introduction: On this second Sunday of Lent, God makes a covenant with Abram and promises him descendants as many as the stars. In the Gospel, Jesus goes up the mountain to pray, and while he prays he is transfigured, and speaks with Moses and Elijah about his departure in Jerusalem. Paul reminds us that our citizenship is in heaven. Let us listen to the beloved Son.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is our light and our salvation. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may listen to the beloved Son and follow him on the way to Jerusalem. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are discouraged on their journey: that a glimpse of Christ's glory may strengthen them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who live only for earthly things: that they may discover that our citizenship is in heaven. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are searching for God's face: that they may find him in prayer. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may make time to climb the mountain of prayer this Lent. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you told us to listen to your beloved Son. Feed us with his word, and purify our hearts so that we may see his glory. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: As he was praying
reflection.body:
God takes Abram outside on a starry night: "Look now toward the sky, and count the stars, if you are able to count them." Then he promises, "So your offspring will be." Abram is old and has no children, but "He believed in the LORD, who credited it to him for righteousness." God then seals a covenant with him in a mysterious ceremony at nightfall.

In Luke's account of the Transfiguration, Jesus takes Peter, John and James up the mountain "to pray." Luke alone tells us that it happened "As he was praying": "the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling." Prayer is where Jesus' glory shines through.

Luke also tells us what Moses and Elijah talk about with him. They "spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem." The Greek word Luke uses is exodus. Jesus is about to lead a new exodus, through his death and Resurrection.

The disciples are "heavy with sleep," but they wake up and see his glory. Peter wants to stay: "Master, it is good for us to be here." Then a cloud overshadows them, and the Father speaks: "This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!" When the voice is gone, "Jesus was found alone." Everything now depends on listening to him.

Paul reminds us where we are heading: "our citizenship is in heaven, from where we also wait for a Savior," who "will change the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of his glory."

Like the disciples, we are often heavy with sleep. This Lent, make time to pray on the mountain: a quiet time each day with the Gospel. Listen to Jesus. And pray the psalm: "The LORD is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear?"
